page: Amazon Web Services c8in.12xlarge is an eighth-generation compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance features a dedicated x86_64 Intel processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. It provides 48 virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with two threads per core, paired with 96.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 2.0 GB per vCPU.

Network performance is a primary characteristic of the c8in family, offering a baseline network throughput of 75 Gbps. This instance configuration does not include local instance storage, requiring network-attached storage via Amazon EBS or remote storage services for persistent data. It does not incorporate discrete hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

The dense compute capacity and 75 Gbps baseline networking make the c8in.12xlarge suitable for distributed compute clusters, high-traffic web serving tiers, continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, and network-intensive workloads that require substantial parallel processing without extensive in-memory footprints.
description: Amazon Web Services c8in.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 3.9 GHz Intel x86_64 processor managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 48 vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, accompanied by 96.0 GB of system memory at an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs present on the host. The instance features a baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps, supporting high-throughput inter-node data exchange. The combination of high-frequency compute resources and 75 Gbps network bandwidth positions this instance for distributed computing tasks, high-capacity API gateways, batch processing jobs, and network-bound application infrastructure.
